title: Breakable Machine: A K–12 Classroom Game for Transformative AI Literacy Through Spoofing and eXplainable AI (XAI)
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the need for K–12 AI literacy experiences that go beyond teaching students how to build or use AI systems and instead help them critically interrogate how AI works, where it fails, and why those failures matter socially. The authors argue that many existing tools emphasize model training and functional success, but fewer resources help learners examine brittleness, bias, adversarial vulnerability, and the sociotechnical nature of AI.

To meet this need, the paper presents “Breakable Machine,” a browser-based classroom game in which students try to spoof an image classifier by changing their appearance or surroundings to trigger high-confidence misclassifications. The game includes an eXplainable AI heat-map view, a shared leaderboard, and access to training data so students can compare strategies, infer what features the model uses, and reflect on why outputs change. The approach is designed for learners aged 10–15 and is intended for use in classroom settings with mobile devices and internet or local network connectivity.

The paper is a non-empirical design and theory paper rather than an evaluation study. It positions the resource as especially suitable for grades 4–9 and for projects that already introduce basic image classification concepts. The authors conclude that spoofing and failure-based activities can support critical and transformative AI literacy by fostering conceptual understanding, ethical awareness, data agency, and collective sensemaking about AI as a fallible sociotechnical system.

identified_tools.name: ITS (General)
identified_tools.description: An intelligent tutoring or instructional AI system that provides adaptive guidance, feedback, or scaffolded learning support.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper describes a browser-based K–12 classroom game, Breakable Machine, designed to teach AI literacy by having students spoof an image classifier and inspect XAI heat maps. It does not evaluate a tutoring system, but it does discuss teaching students about AI systems generally.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a non-empirical design/resource paper. It proposes a classroom game and pedagogical rationale but reports no study, no sample, and no measured outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: No impact data are reported, so there is no measurable evidence of learning gains or other effects.
